text:
nishant: paging: multiple containers in us-west-2 serving pool A restarted due to GPU OOM during prefill. customer impact flagged for a handful of high-throughput customers.

eva: seeing repeated SIGKILL on vektra-gpu-3, logs show prefill size spikes ~1.2M tokens on some requests.

sam: oncall here. thanks for the ping — taking ownership. can you paste a sample stack / prefill trace?

nishant: pasted from node: 
```
2024-10-05T03:21:10Z runtime ERROR: CUDA out of memory while materializing KV cache. prefill_len=980000, batch=1, model=gptx-13b-q4
Container restart triggered by oom-killer
```

eva: most of these originate from a single API key that has started sending very long system prompts and context windows. looks like no prefix trimming at client side.

incident-bot: incident created: INC-2024-5739. severity: P2. Pager duty notified.

pagerduty: page sent to ops-oncall (sam). escalation policy = gpu-prefill.

sam: quick mitigation ideas: 1) enable prefill-length cap at edge (short-term, 30s change) 2) route long-context requests to low-memory fallback (quantized small model) 3) scale up pool A with spare nodes if available.

kate: we have 2 spare g5 nodes in us-west-2 standby group. can spin them up, but provisioning ~6m.

eva: can we push a routing rule: if prefill_tokens > 200k -> route to dedicated-hotfallback model (gptx-13b-q4-small) and return a structured warning to client? that should prevent OOMs.

sam: agree. eva, can you push the routing rule? i'll coordinate the client-facing rate-limiter and prefill cap.

eva: making change now. will update traffic router with rule and a short circuit that rejects >1M tokens outright with 413 + retry-after.

nishant: also enabling aggressive KV cache eviction for new requests to reduce resident memory during prefill. patch rolling to pool A.

incident-bot: runbook step executed: enable-prefill-throttle applied by eva at 1738010200.

sam: temporary customer message draft: "We're investigating increased failures for very large context requests. We've applied mitigations to route extremely large prompts to a safer fallback and are limiting prefill sizes. If you rely on >500k contexts, please contact support for a dedicated capacity option." Thoughts?

kate: good. add ETA for full fix: we expect stable routing + node scale in ~10-15m, full follow-up after postmortem.

eva: routing rule live at 1738010400. I see a reduction in restarts immediately. still a couple of stragglers hitting mid-sized prefill spikes.

sam: spun up one spare node; provisioning healthy at 1738011800. will keep autoscaler watching.

nishant: customer impact: ~8 customers saw transient 5xx in last 30m, two reported degraded latency but no data loss. marked for customer ops outreach.

sam: leaving oncall bridge for now. hand off to night shift @kate in 20m. will update INC ticket with timeline and mitigation steps.

kate: taking over. please add me to the incident ticket.

incident-bot: incident INC-2024-5739 status: mitigated -> partial, assigned -> kate, next update expected in 30m.

nishant: follow-up actions: 1) enforce prefill soft cap at edge SDK (engineering) 2) add server-side short-circuit for >1M tokens (prod) 3) customer comms and offer dedicated capacity for heavy contexts (support/sales) 4) postmortem scheduled.

sam: thanks all. closing slack bridge for now, keep updates in INC ticket. :thumbsup:
